runtime_status: runtime-evidenced on Windows PowerShell 5.1: every MCP server in three live provider configs completed a real initialize -> tools/list exchange, and the three dead command paths found there were repaired and re-verified. Linux/static/artifact gates pass in CI.
notes: v7.9.8: make the agent pick the strongest capability that already exists instead of rebuilding a weaker one, and repair the fresh-install path that contradicted the bundle's own decisions. The audit came first and found the reported defect plus three nobody had reported. The Hermes portable starter shipped a live mcp_servers block with five servers -- context7, sequential-thinking, @modelcontextprotocol/server-github@2025.4.8, @playwright/mcp@latest and firecrawl-mcp -- while its own README said 'Empty mcp_servers' and its own header said the file must never contain a live MCP command. Because Install-Provider-Starter-Settings.ps1 copies the file whole onto a machine with no config.yaml, every entry was a fresh-install default: sequential-thinking after 7.9.7 measured it out of the always-on core, a package npm marks no longer supported, an unpinned server that can change its tool surface mid-session, and an extras-only server that made -WithExtras meaningless for Hermes. Root cause fixed at the source (mcp_servers: {}) rather than by cleaning up after the copy, and Install-Provider-Starter-Settings.ps1 now refuses the SHAPE -- any starter declaring live MCP entries in YAML, TOML or JSON, or any @latest package -- so the four symptoms cannot return individually. Also found by the same audit: capability-profiles still called sequential-thinking one of 'the always-on three' after 7.9.7 demoted it, the Hermes README was wrong about reasoning_effort, max_turns and the compression threshold as well as MCP, and final_pack_version sat in 37 skills where nothing read it and 36 had drifted to 4.3.0/5.0.0/5.1.0 inside a 7.9.x pack -- removed, with a contract forbidding its return, because VERSION.txt is the single authority. The routing work was decided by measurement, not preference: Hermes v0.20.4 ships web_search/web_extract over a keyless vendor ring (exa, parallel, tavily, firecrawl, keenable) with round-robin and rate-limit failover, verified by running it keylessly at 1.4s search and 0.7s extract, while firecrawl-mcp costs 25 tool schemas and 36,337 bytes (~9,084 tokens on every turn, eight times the server 7.9.7 removed for being too expensive) and keylessly answers only search and scrape -- map, crawl, agent and interact each return 'API key is required', verified by calling them. So the expensive surface duplicated the native one and its unique half needed an account this pack refuses by default. One new skill, capability-routing, added only after auditing capability-profiles, tool-discovery, ai-tooling-stack, research-verification, tool-output-awareness and assumption-audit: the nearest owner triggers on enabling MCP servers, and a model about to write a Node crawler never matches that description, which is decisive because these skills load by description. research-verification gained the escalation principle at its own seam rather than a clone. TOOLS/Measure-McpSchemaCost.ps1 ships the measurement 7.9.7 asserted but could not reproduce. 146 canonical skills across 5 provider trees; no new always-on MCP, and none added to any provider by default.
